items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He got on the phone right away and called his manager who’s now Harold Loxley. Man, that Harold Loxley – good guy, nice man.

ctx.x: What inspired you to have to go back and study?

Well I’ll tell you, the things I wanted to do. The things I wanted to do, I needed more studying and I was – I was branching into harmonies that I had introduced to jazz. For instance, while I was with Lunceford’s band, one day I introduced a chord called the thirteenth with the augmented eleventh. And this became the ending chord for everybody. Everybody copied that one chord then. And when I wrote it for Duke and them, I wrote out the – I wrote that one, but then I threw in another one that I had been playing…
Okay. Ken just handed me the um, publication of Yard Dog Mazurka…
